policies.title: Uzbek passport: citizenship
policies.summary: An Uzbek citizen has a constitutional right to return to Uzbekistan without hindrance.
conditions: This scope does not model internal-document, residence, exit, border-pass, or special-document rules for Uzbek citizens.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: unlimited visa-free entry
policies.summary: Uzbekistan's current MFA procedure lists these bilateral ordinary-passport visa-free regimes without a stated time limit.
conditions: The government MFA page lists these bilateral regimes as unlimited. All-passport and purpose language is specific to the bilateral group; ordinary passports are modeled here.
A valid travel document and border admission remain required; stateless residents, work/residence, and special-document treatment are not inferred.

policies.title: Kyrgyz ordinary passports: 60-day visa-free entry
policies.summary: The MFA procedure lists Kyrgyz citizens for visa-free stays of up to 60 days.
conditions: The current MFA list specifies up to 60 days. Longer stay requires the applicable entry visa; normal border admission remains required.

policies.title: Tajik ordinary passports: 30-day visa-free entry
policies.summary: The MFA procedure lists Tajik citizens for visa-free stays of up to 30 days.
conditions: The current MFA list specifies up to 30 days. Longer stay requires the applicable entry visa; normal border admission remains required.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: 30-day visa-free entry
policies.summary: The current MFA procedure lists these ordinary-passport nationalities for visa-free entry up to 30 days.
conditions: The general 30-day regime begins upon border crossing; expiry requires departure or a suitable entry visa. The page describes travel-document and admission requirements.

China and Qatar also appear in the page's conditional 10-day air-ticket note. The MFA page is internally inconsistent for those two ordinary-passport routes, so this policy normalizes only visa-free status.
Hong Kong and Macao are expressly included in the 30-day PRC-and-SAR list. The separate 10-day note names China but does not name either SAR.

policies.title: Bahraini, Kuwaiti and Omani ordinary passports: conditional 10-day visa-free entry
policies.summary: The MFA page specifically grants up to 10 visa-free days to these citizens with an onward air ticket.
conditions: Requires an air ticket to the home country or a third country. The MFA page does not establish work, residence, transit, diplomatic/official, or special-document treatment.
Passport validity, security screening, and border admission remain applicable.

policies.title: Live official selector: listed ordinary passports' eVisa
policies.summary: The live official eVisa selector assigns the online 30-day eVisa route to these ordinary-passport nationalities.
conditions: The official selector assigns these nationalities status 1, and its official status endpoint defines status 1 as a 30-day visa with three-working-day processing. This resolves the MFA Appendix 1 ‘eVisa or simplified consular tourist visa’ ambiguity for these specific selector records.
The selector also labels Hong Kong status 1, but the current MFA schedule expressly puts Hong Kong in the 30-day PRC-and-SAR visa-free group; this policy therefore does not include Hong Kong.
Apply through the official eVisa portal using the travel document used for entry. The portal requires a passport and electronic visa at the border; a refusal remains possible under Uzbek law.
This policy is only for ordinary passports and does not establish work, residence, diplomatic/official, special-document, airport-issuance, or transit rights.

application.label: Official electronic visa portal of the Republic of Uzbekistan
application.processingTime: Three working days according to the live selector status definition.
steps: Select the nationality, ordinary travel document, purpose, and intended dates in the official portal.
Enter biographical data, upload the photo and passport data page, activate the request, and pay the consular fee.
Receive the outcome by email and carry the electronic visa with the same travel document used for the application.

policies.title: Portal-absent ordinary passports: advance consular visa
policies.summary: These ordinary passports are neither in the current visa-free schedules nor in the live eVisa selector, so the MFA’s advance consular-visa rule applies.
conditions: The MFA states that foreign citizens need an entry visa unless listed in its visa-free regimes. The official eVisa portal directs a nationality outside its simplified list to the appropriate MFA foreign institution.

The ordinary consular process requires advance MFA visa confirmation based on an invitation-application. Tashkent-airport issuance is not a general visa-on-arrival route: it also requires an inviting party’s advance confirmation.

This policy does not convert the separate five-day Uzbekistan Airways transit programme into a nationality-wide visitor status and does not cover work, residence, diplomatic/official, or special-document routes.

unresolved.reason: Kosovo is absent from the MFA visa-free schedules and the live eVisa selector. The general foreigner-visa framework does not directly establish Uzbekistan's treatment of a Kosovo ordinary passport, so no route is inferred.

Taiwan is neither separately named in the MFA visa-free schedules nor represented in the live eVisa selector. The PRC/Hong Kong/Macao wording does not directly establish treatment of a Taiwan ordinary passport, so no route is inferred.

The current MFA schedule excludes Saudi Arabia from its visa-free list and puts it in the eVisa-or-simplified-consular appendix, while the live official eVisa selector labels it visa-free for 30 days. The direct official sources conflict, so no status is inferred.
